earlier_scan.source_named: Hendon, Rufus S. 1966. The Phonology and Morphology of Ulu Muar Malay (Kuala Pilah District, Negri Sembilan, Malaya). Yale University Publications in Anthropology 70.
earlier_scan.note: Full phonology of a Negeri Sembilan variety exists; archive.org copy (phonologymorphol0000rufu) is access-restricted; also Asmah Haji Omar 2015 phonology pages 358-371.

sources.citation: Ogloblin, A.K. 1986. Some problems of diachronic typology of the Malayo-Javanic languages. In Geraghty, Carrington & Wurm (eds), FOCAL II: Papers from the Fourth International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics (Pacific Linguistics C-94), 111-122. DOI 10.15144/PL-C94.111
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 117 (read from a rendered page image): 'As for delimitative stress, it does not seem to be quite the same in the different languages of the group. In particular, diphthongisation of vowels in the final syllable in Mkb, Peninsular Mal and Ac may, according to some authors, Cowan among them, be linked with stress movement (delimitative, not phonological) to this syllable.' General remark on Peninsular Malay dialects, not specific to Ulu Muar/Negeri Sembilan; Hendon 1966 cited only for segmental alternations (pp. 116-117).

sources.citation: Winstedt, R.O. 1913. Malay grammar. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (archive.org malaygrammar00winsrich)
sources.note: sec. 14 'Accent' is a statement about Malay in general (penultimate unless the penult is an open syllable with short vowel); no Negri Sembilan / Minangkabau-dialect stress statement.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Negeri Sembilan Malay' and (ms) 'Bahasa Melayu Negeri Sembilan'
sources.note: Neither page discusses stress or intonation; references list Asmah 2015, Reniwati 2012, Idris Aman et al. 2016/2019, Hendon 1966 (further reading).

sources.citation: Idris Aman, Mohammad Fadzeli Jaafar & Norsimah Mat Awal. 2019. Language and identity: a reappraisal of Negeri Sembilan Malay language. Kajian Malaysia 37(1): 27-49. DOI 10.21315/km2019.37.1.2
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segmental pronunciation test (17 vowel/consonant features vs Minangkabau); nothing on stress. Its literature review (pp. 29-30) lists the phonological descriptions of the dialect: Hendon 1966, Sharman 1973/1974, Mohd Pilus 1978, Yeop Johari 1984, Asmah 1985, Ibrahim & Ibrahim 1990, Arbak 1994, Ajid 2002, Reniwati 1990 (full references pp. 46-49).
